All figures were read this session from the EDGAR documents themselves: the FY2024 Form 10-K (accession 0001326801-25-000017) and the 2025 proxy statement (DEF 14A, accession 0001326801-25-000040, record date April 1, 2025); this replaces the pilot's unverified WebFetch summary and the investor-CDN PDF. OWNERSHIP: the proxy gives Zuckerberg 141,000 Class A shares (marked * for less than 1% of Class A), 342,606,985 Class B shares (99.8% of Class B) and 61.0% of total voting power, but no percentage of all shares, so pctEconomic is null and the 13.58% economic share is in leader.derived (both class counts quoted). Footnote (2): the holding consists of 3,388,097 Class B shares held by the Mark Zuckerberg Trust; 192,874,288 Class B held by CZI Holdings, LLC; 34,344,500 by Chan Zuckerberg Holdings LLC; 12,000,000 by CZI Holdings I, LLC (pledged as collateral for indebtedness); 50,000,000 each by Chan Zuckerberg Holdings II and III, LLC; 100 by CZ Management, LLC; and 141,000 Class A held by the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative Foundation, over which he has sole voting and investment power 'but no pecuniary interest'. No options or RSUs are included. A shareholder proposal printed in the proxy says he owns '14% of the economic value'; that is the proponent's statement, not the company's, and is not used. 5% HOLDERS: the proxy states their percentages as % of Class A only (Vanguard 8.5%, BlackRock 7.2%, FMR 6.1%), and those are the figures recorded in pctEconomic. On an all-shares basis they would be lower (Class B is about 13.6% of all shares); they are not recomputed, per the no-derivation rule. Their total-voting-power percentages are 3.3%, 2.8% and 2.4%. The proxy footnotes cite only the Schedule 13G/A filing dates (Feb 9-13, 2024), not the ownership dates, so holder asOf is omitted; the share counts are stale relative to the April 1, 2025 denominator. CASH: buybacks are cash paid in 2024 ($30,125m); the equity statement's value of shares repurchased ($29,754m) is a different basis. Dividends include dividend equivalents on RSUs. GEOGRAPHY: Europe includes Russia and Turkey; Rest of World includes Africa, Latin America and the Middle East (10-K footnote 3); United States alone was $59.73 billion (footnote 1). No employee stock purchase plan appears in the 10-K, so plan is null.

studies.title: Meta's Economic Contribution in the U.S. (2024)

ecosystem.notes: The 10-K has no flow measure, so measure is null. The study is Meta's own ("a new study we conducted", announced May 13, 2025) and covers the U.S. only. It starts from Meta's estimate that each U.S. ad dollar yields $3.71 of advertiser revenue ("over $215 billion in business/advertisers revenues in the U.S. from Meta ads"), then applies BEA input-output multipliers for indirect and induced activity, so the $548 billion is a modelled economic-activity figure, not money paid to businesses or creators. It includes about $2 billion of Meta's own non-advertising sales. A separate Meta study puts the EU figure at €213 billion and 1.44 million jobs in 2024; it is not added here. Meta revenue is worldwide, so it is not comparable with the U.S.-only study figure.
